# Buying-agent first look — list + template

_Created 2026-08-29 (decision 3 of the £2M+ / Keyhole proposal). Founder
action, not code: this channel is a relationship, run by email._

## What this is

Buying agents (Domus Holmes, Black Brick, Property Vision and their peers)
are retained by families to FIND houses. Their scarcest input is
off-market supply. Our refurbished exits are exactly that: finished period
family houses, chain-free, with a completed project behind them.

The first look gives a vetted circle of buy-side agents early sight of an
exit before open marketing. It costs us nothing we value (we want buyers),
and it builds the relationship that brings their surplus intelligence back:
the probate wreck that fits no client brief of theirs is our deal.

## The one rule: asymmetry

**Buy-side agents never see our sourcing.** Not the distress lists, not the
probate pipeline, not scout leads, not anything a competitor for stock
could act on. What flows outward is finished stock and address-level
analytics on properties THEY already hold. What flows inward is whatever
they choose to send. If a first-look agent asks where we find our
projects, the answer is a smile.

## Who gets on the list

- Buy-side only. An agent who also lists property for sellers is a
  conflict, not a partner.
- Active London family-house briefs in or near our districts.
- Vetted by a real conversation first. The founder decides; nobody joins
  by asking.
- Off the list on the first leak of a first-look property to open channels.

Keep the list itself in the CRM or a simple sheet: firm, contact, brief
profile, districts, date added, deals shown, outcomes.

## Email template — first look on an exit

Subject: **First look: [street], [district] — before it goes to market**

> Hi [name],
>
> Before we instruct an agent, a first look for your clients.
>
> **[Address line], [District]**
> [X]-bed [Victorian/Edwardian] [terrace/semi], fully refurbished this
> year. [One line on the work: rewired, replumbed, new kitchen and
> bathrooms, loft, garden.] Chain-free: we own it, there is nothing to
> wait for.
>
> Guide: £[figure]. EPC [band]. Floor plan and photos attached.
>
> The first look closes on [date]. After that it goes to open market.
> If a client fits, come and see it this week. If not, no reply needed.
>
> [Founder name]
> Kept · wearekept.co.uk

Rules for the template:

- A real date on the first-look window, always. A window with no end is
  marketing noise.
- The guide is a sale price for stock we own. That is ordinary commerce;
  the no-figure rule governs offers to vendors, not our own exits.
- No urgency theatre. One email, one date, no follow-up chase.
- Voice per `docs/brand/KEPT.md`: short declaratives, no em dashes, no
  exclamation marks.

## What we offer them beyond stock (later, once Keyhole exists)

Address-level analytics on properties they already hold for clients:
condition and cost context, conservation-area and Article 4 flags. Keyhole
(`/keyhole`) is the vehicle: it works on any address they type, it never
shows them our pipeline, and every report is a reason to talk to us.

## What we never do

- Never pay for an introduction without a written agreement reviewed
  first (SRA and RICS rules bind the professionals; see the PRD's open
  questions).
- Never give exclusivity on the list itself. First look is a window, not
  an option.
- Never let this channel slow an exit: if the window lapses, it lists.
